title: RFC 7489 - Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
summary: Defines domain-level authentication policy mechanisms for senders to publish how receivers should handle unauthenticated emails claiming to be from their domain.
key_invariants: Alignment: DMARC requires that the From header domain matches either the authenticated SPF domain (Return-Path) or the authenticated DKIM domain (d= tag).

Strict vs Relaxed Mode: Under relaxed alignment (aspf=r, adkim=r), subdomains match the organizational parent (e.g., mail.corp.com matches corp.com). Under strict alignment (aspf=s, adkim=s), exact domain string matching is enforced.
Policy Modes: p=none (monitoring only, no rejection), p=quarantine (deliver to junk folder), p=reject (strictly bounce/drop message at SMTP edge).
forensic_guidance: If an email fails SPF and DKIM alignment against the visible From header, DMARC validation fails. A receiver adhering to RFC 7489 MUST apply the published policy action.

title: RFC 7208 - Sender Policy Framework (SPF)
summary: Allows domain owners to publish lists of IP addresses and CIDR subnets authorized to send emails on behalf of their domain.
key_invariants: Evaluated Identity: SPF evaluates the envelope sender (SMTP MAIL FROM / Return-Path), NOT the RFC 5322 visible From header.
ESP Relay Forwarding: Third-party email services (SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES) stamp their own Return-Path domain (e.g., bounces.sendgrid.net) which passes SPF independently of the sender domain.
Lookup Limit: SPF evaluation must not exceed 10 DNS queries (including 'include', 'a', 'mx', 'ptr', 'exists'). Exceeding 10 queries results in a PermError.
forensic_guidance: SPF pass alone does NOT guarantee authenticity of the visible From header; DMARC domain alignment is mandatory to verify that SPF authoritatively covers the sender identity.

title: RFC 6376 - DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) Signatures
summary: Cryptographically signs email headers and body using an asymmetric public/private key pair published via DNS TXT records.
key_invariants: Canonicalization: Specifies whitespace and casing normalization ('simple' vs 'relaxed') for header (c=relaxed/relaxed) and body.
Domain Tag (d=): Specifies the domain taking responsibility for the signature. Must match the visible From domain for DMARC alignment.
Selector (s=): Specifies the DNS record prefix where the public RSA/Ed25519 key is fetched (selector._domainkey.domain).
forensic_guidance: A valid DKIM signature proves that the signed headers and body hash were not altered in transit since signing by the key owner.

title: RFC 5322 - Internet Message Format (MIME & Envelope Headers)
summary: Defines the standard syntax and structure for electronic mail messages, mandatory header fields, and relay Received tracing.
key_invariants: Chronology: Each intermediate MTA prepends a 'Received:' header at the very top. Hop analysis must be read from bottom (origin) to top (destination).
Timestamp Invariant: Timestamps in the Received chain must be strictly monotonically non-decreasing. Any negative latency indicates clock desynchronization or forged relay headers.
From vs Reply-To: 'From' specifies author; 'Reply-To' specifies destination for responses. Mismatched organizational domains indicate potential fraud or legitimate mailing lists.
forensic_guidance: Always compute delta T between consecutive hops to identify forged headers and analyze originating IP from the bottom-most public hop.
